ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a ring network formed by connecting transformers of different voltage levels. The top bus is marked 220 kV. The left branch has a transformer marked 220/38.5 kV, directly connected to the lower low-voltage ring-network side marked 35 kV. The right alternative branch first passes through a transformer marked 220/121 kV, connects to a middle line marked 110 kV, then passes through a transformer on the right marked 110/38.5 kV, and finally also connects to the same 35 kV ring-network side. Reasoning: Convert both paths from the 220 kV side to the 35 kV side and compare them. The induced voltage on the low-voltage side of the left path is 220 × 38.5/220 = 38.5 kV. The right path passes through two stages of transformation, 220/121 kV and 110/38.5 kV, and the converted low-voltage-side voltage is 220 × 121/220 × 38.5/110 = 42.35 kV. The voltages given by the two paths on the same 35 kV ring-network side are not equal, so there is a voltage difference in the closed ring network, which will produce circulating power. The induced voltage corresponding to the right 35 kV side is higher, so the power flows from right to left on the lower 35 kV line, then returns through the left transformer and the upper/right path, and according to the loop direction in the figure, it is judged to be clockwise circulation.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the left branch transformer as 220/38.5 kV and the alternate right branch as the series combination 220/121 kV followed by 110/38.5 kV, both tying into the same 35 kV ring. Then refer both paths to the 35 kV side. The left path gives 220 × 38.5/220 = 38.5 kV. The right path gives 220 × 121/220 × 38.5/110 = 42.35 kV. Since these two voltages are not equal, a voltage difference exists around the closed ring, so circulating power exists. The right-hand 35 kV side is at the higher induced voltage, so current/power flows along the lower 35 kV side from right to left and returns through the left transformer and upper/right path; as drawn, this is clockwise circulation.
